newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica reports surplus despite trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica reports surplus despite trade deficit.

text.p: Jamaica's central bank said Wednesday that the country's balance of payments was US$245.8 million in surplus for the first eight months of this year, despite the fact that the trade balance hit a record deficit of US$911.7 million over the same period.

The payments surplus was fueled by continued strong inflows in remittances from Jamaicans overseas, plus increases in tourism inflows and overseas borrowing to fund the import bill, the bank said. The payments surplus as of August 1995 was US$13.3 million.
Remittances stood at US$287.9 million, down US$45.7 million from the US$333.6 million recorded August last year, but tourism earnings US$59.5 million to US$682.4 million for the same period.

Private capital flows in the form of loans and investment in tourism projects rose from US$108.3 million to US$394.5 million. The increased lending is being blamed for pushing the import bill to US$1.85 billion, double the country's export earnings over the eight month period.
The strong inflows continue to bolster Jamaica's net international reserves, which at the end of October stood at US$658 million.
